answer: One identity stakes one canyon quartz vein and locks a 70-credit bond. A raven survey flight logs width, depth, coordinates with a key-signed chip. An auditor recomputes it from the quartz-vein survey table: width or depth 5% off, a reused survey, or a double claim burns the bond. The first claim costs 34 credits; the kth costs 34+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5029 and 1,000 fakes pay 2,531,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-survey ring fails: a reused flight log cannot match new coordinates or timestamp. An honest staker pays 34 once, recovering the bond after a clean epoch.
